deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the second page (verso) of an administrative letter from the Institut de France, Académie des Sciences, dated Paris, 24 March 1875. It is addressed to Friedrich Wöhler in Göttingen, who was a foreign associate of the Académie. The first page (previous folio) says the Académie is sending, at Wöhler's request of 3 March, the original manuscript Riemann submitted to the Académie's 1861 prize competition on the heat state of an infinite homogeneous solid body. This page continues from the previous one, which ended 'Les règlements de l'Académie s'opposent, Monsieur,':

(1) The Académie's regulations oppose any communication of this kind. However, the aim pursued by Professor Weber is too praiseworthy for the Académie to withhold its help. Weber, assisted by Dedekind, was then preparing Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke (1876).
(2) The Académie expresses its full confidence and relies on Wöhler's discretion to make the best use of the memoir, and asks for an acknowledgement of receipt.
(3) Once printing is finished, the original manuscript is to be returned so that it can go back into the Académie's archives at once.
(4) Closing formula. Signed 'Pour le Secrétaire perpétuel et par autorisation' by an official of the secretariat. The signature reads as Maindron, most likely Ernest Maindron, the Académie's secretariat archivist.

The next page is Wöhler's covering letter of 26 March 1875 forwarding the manuscript to Weber. It credits the concession to J.-B. Dumas, the Secrétaire perpétuel, and asks Weber to return the manuscript directly to the Académie.

Historical significance: the page documents how the text of Riemann's 1861 Paris prize essay ('Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae') was obtained for its first publication in the Werke of 1876. That essay contains Riemann's treatment of quadratic differential forms and the curvature condition for flatness. Nothing is derived or computed on this page itself.

results.what: Archival/provenance record: the Paris Académie lent Riemann's 1861 prize-competition manuscript (heat conduction) to Göttingen in March 1875, via Wöhler, for Weber's edition of Riemann's collected works.
results.usually_credited_to: Publication credited to H. Weber (with R. Dedekind), Riemann's Gesammelte Werke, 1876

deep.surprise_reason: The page is administrative correspondence with no mathematical content. That Weber obtained the Paris prize essay from the Académie for the 1876 Werke is known; the letter only adds procedural detail about the loan.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription matches the image well.
Signature: the initial is unclear and could be 'E.' rather than 'G.'. The signer is very likely Ernest Maindron of the Académie's secretariat, so 'E. Maindron' is the probable reading.
'Monsieur et Illustre Confrère': the image shows the ampersand-like 'et' written as 'et'; the reading is correct.
